mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Dedicated Palletizing Cell and a Centralized Multi-Line System?

acceptedAnswer.text: A dedicated cell palletizes one line, at the end of that line. A centralized system brings several lines to one palletizing area through conveying, merging and accumulation. TRFSpeed scales from a dedicated cell to a centralized multi-line system, which suits chemical plants with several packaging lines. TRF validates the combined rate and case mix before quoting.

mainEntity.name: What Is Slip Sheet Palletizing and When Is It Needed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Slip sheet palletizing places a sheet of paperboard or plastic under the first layer or between layers to stabilize the load and protect the units. It is specified for loads that shift. TRFSpeed supports slip sheet handling, automatic pallet handling and pallet discharge, and your pallet specification defines when the sheets are used.

mainEntity.name: Can a Compact Palletizer Be Installed in a Brownfield Plant With Limited Space?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. TRFCompact puts an industrial robot in a compact standardized cell designed for brownfield plants where floor space is a major limitation, and it keeps multiple SKU recipes and pallet patterns. TRF lays out the cell, the infeed and the pallet exchange around your columns, aisles and forklift paths during the application review.

mainEntity.name: How Many Cases per Minute Can a Robotic Palletizer Handle?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the platform. TRFCobot covers about 1 to 10 cases per minute, TRFCompact about 5 to 15 and TRFSpeed about 10 to 35. These are typical ranges for commercial screening: TRF confirms the final rate for your cases, end-of-arm tool, pallet pattern and reach, and loads outside the ranges are reviewed by TRF engineering.

mainEntity.name: How Is Payback Calculated for Chemical Palletizing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payback depends on the labor hours the palletizer replaces, shifts per day, local labor cost and the installed cost of the system. The estimate divides the system cost, including maintenance, by the annual net savings: the labor cost of manual palletizing minus the electricity the robot uses. Long continuous runs keep utilization high. The payback calculator returns a first estimate.
